transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Rachel Nguyen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (AtlasPay Head of IT), Luca Bianchi (AtlasPay Security Engineer), Emma Chen (AtlasPay Legal), Omar Khalid (AtlasPay Compliance)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Samir, AE on the account, and Rachel is our solutions engineer. Today we wanted to run through data residency, region pinning, and any compliance questions you have, especially around EU/US cross-border.

[00:22] Marta: Thanks. We just want to make sure our EU payments data stays in the EU, and that there is clear documentation for subprocessors. Also curious about key management - we might need BYOK.

[00:35] Rachel: Great, we can walk through how Redwood handles region pinning. For hosted customers we support region selection per project and prefer eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for EU workloads. We do automatic routing to that region, and we have controls to avoid cross-border fallbacks unless explicitly allowed.

[01:05] Luca: When you say "avoid fallbacks", is that a hard guarantee or best-effort? For regulatory audits we need the data to never leave the EU.

[01:15] Rachel: That's a good question. For hosted we provide region pinning with strict routing policies. However, there are edge cases like cold-starts and failover where replica fallback to another region could happen, we treat those as measurable events. For stricter guarantees we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with region-only capacity which avoids cross-region routing.

[02:00] Samir: To add, we have contractual language in the DPA for region commitments and can add clauses for mandatory notification of cross-border processing. Also we support standard contractual clauses (SCCs) for EU data transfers.

[02:20] Emma: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO27001 certifications? We'll need the attestations and some supporting evidence for our vendor assessment.

[02:30] Samir: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001. I'll send the latest attestations and our security pack after the call.

[03:10] Luca: OK, key management - is BYOK supported for hosted? Can we control keys in our KMS?

[03:22] Rachel: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for major clouds. We also offer HSM-backed key options for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted BYOK, we surface a key binding that keeps data encrypted at rest with your key; however some metadata and logs are still managed by the platform unless you choose Private.

[04:00] Marta: And encryption in transit? TLS and mTLS?

[04:07] Rachel: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ by default. For Private deployments we can enable mutual TLS between customer network and Redwood control plane.

[04:30] Omar: Subprocessors - who are your subprocessors and are any located outside the EU? For compliance we need a full list and geolocation.

[04:40] Samir: We can share the subprocessors list. Major ones include cloud providers (GCP/AWS), telemetry providers, and observability vendors. For EU-region pinning we'll ensure that compute and storage are in the EU, but some support vendors may operate outside EU; we surface that in the subprocessor list and can add contract language.

[05:15] Luca: For Schrems II concerns, do you recommend SCCs or do you offer other mitigations?

[05:25] Rachel: SCCs are standard and we can incorporate them into the DPA. We also provide architectural mitigations: minimizing exported data, encrypting with customer-managed keys so the provider doesn't have plaintext access, and logging controls. If you're highly regulated, Private deployment avoids many cross-border vendor issues.

[06:10] Marta: What about audit logs? Can we export them to our SIEM? Retention windows?

[06:22] Samir: Yes, audit logs are available and can be exported to customer SIEM via S3 or streaming. Default retention is 90 days in hosted; we can negotiate retention in contract or enable longer retention for Dedicated/Private. Logs include request-level metadata, user and service identities, and timestamps.

[07:05] Emma: Are logs pseudonymized? We need to ensure PII is not inadvertently stored in logs.

[07:15] Rachel: We scrub user-provided content from certain logs and can configure redaction. For strict PII policies we recommend routing user content through customer-managed storage or using Private deployment to keep content on-prem.

[08:00] Luca: Can you detail the region pinning configuration? Is it at the project level, org level, or per-endpoint?

[08:12] Rachel: It's configurable at the workspace/project level. You can pin projects to a region and also set fallback policies - strict (no fallback), soft (fallback with notification), or hybrid. The strict mode is only available with Dedicated/Private at the moment for complete isolation.

[09:00] Marta: Cost tradeoffs? If we pick strict EU-only routing and BYOK, any predictable cost increase?

[09:10] Samir: There's usually a delta for Dedicated or Private deployments (reserved capacity or on-prem). For hosted with BYOK, there's minimal per-request overhead, but if we need dedicated EU-only capacity to meet SLOs that will be priced as reserved capacity. We'll put numbers in the pilot quote.

[10:05] Luca: About subprocessors again - if a subprocessor changes, what's the notification timeline?

[10:15] Samir: Standard is 30 days notice for subprocessor changes and we can add stricter notification in the contract.

[11:00] Emma: Data deletion - how fast can you delete EU customer data if required? Is there a hard delete?

[11:10] Rachel: We support data deletion requests via API and through the Console. Deletion is usually completed within 7-30 days depending on backups and retention windows; for Private deployments we can adjust to meet your SLA. We also provide a deletion certificate upon completion if required.

[12:00] Marta: One more - can we get a technical runbook of how region pinning is enforced and any telemetry we can audit?

[12:10] Samir: Yes, we'll share a short architecture doc and runbook that describes routing, failover behavior, and available telemetry hooks for audit.

[13:00] Rachel: Quick note on cross-border processing for embeddings: when we compute embeddings for EU data, the model execution may be colocated in the pinned region, but some model variants or third-party accelerators may have constraints. We'll list supported models for EU pinning in the doc.

[14:00] Luca: If we do a pilot, can we test with a sample workload and run a location-specific benchmark?

[14:10] Rachel: Absolutely. For pilots we typically run a small workload in your pinned region and collect latency/throughput and cost metrics. I'll prepare a benchmark plan.

[15:20] Marta: What about legal - do you accept SCCs as-is or do we need to negotiate?

[15:30] Emma: (interjects) We'll review but usually want small edits around liability and deletion timelines.

[16:00] Samir: We can share a DPA with SCCs and common negotiated redlines. We'll work with your legal team.

[17:00] Rachel: Quick caveat - some telemetry and managed services (e.g., error reporting) may be in different regions; we can either disable those or route telemetry to your chosen region depending on the service.

[18:00] Omar: Is there support for dedicated EU-only monitoring stack? We want logs not routed outside.

[18:10] Samir: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can provision an EU-only observability stack. For hosted we have options to stream logs to your EU S3 bucket or SIEM.

[19:30] Marta: Great. So action items?

[19:38] Samir: I'll send SOC2/ISO and the DPA template. Rachel will run the EU benchmark and prepare a runbook and list of supported models for EU pinning. You (AtlasPay) will return subprocessors list and preferred region.

[20:00] Rachel: I'll include config snippets for strict vs soft pinning and a sample terraform snippet for Dedicated if you want to preview.

[20:30] Luca: Regarding BYOK - what KMS do you integrate with?

[20:35] Rachel: We integrate with AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For HSM/BYOK we support customer HSMs in Private deployments. We'll note the exact integration steps in the runbook.

[22:00] Emma: One last question on certification - is there a SOC 2 bridge letter if our assessment needs a current snapshot?

[22:10] Samir: We can provide a bridge letter and attestations. I'll attach them to the email post-call.

[23:00] Marta: Sounds good. If hosted can't meet strict no-cross-border requirement we'll evaluate Dedicated/Private. What's the rough lead time for Dedicated?

[23:12] Samir: Dedicated lead time is typically 4-8 weeks depending on capacity, and Private/on-prem is longer (depends on procurement and network setup). We'll run timelines in the pilot plan.

[24:00] Rachel: I'll prepare the benchmark plan and the architecture runbook.

[25:00] Samir: OK let's recap quickly - next steps are: Samir sends security artifacts and DPA, Rachel sends benchmark/runbook/config snippets, AtlasPay returns subprocessors and region preference. We'll schedule follow-up week of 2026-07-27 to review DPA and pilot terms.

[25:40] Marta: Great, thanks.

[25:45] Emma: Thanks all.

[25:50] Luca: Thanks, bye.

[25:55] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

(End of transcript)
